references.text: The Lord set his heart on your fathers and loved them, and he chose their descendants after them, you, above all peoples, as it is today.
Because he loved your fathers and chose their descendants after them, he brought you out of Egypt himself with his great power.
God's promise to Abraham to make him a great nation shows God's sovereign choice, independent of size or merit.
Israel is called God's servant, the offspring of Jacob whom he chose, the descendants of Abraham whom he loved.
The Lord chose Israel as his people to proclaim his praise, a people he created for himself.
When Israel was young, the Lord loved him and called his son out of Egypt - God's love as the basis for election.
Paul explains that God's choice is not based on works but on the one who calls, referring to Jacob and Esau.
A remnant has been chosen by grace, not by works - God's sovereign choice continues.
God chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world; in love he predestined us to be his children.
God chose what is weak and despised in the world, so that no one may boast before him.
